title: Runtime Configuration
description: The thin bootstrap that tells the system what exists in this environment. Four fields, one file, describes the environment not the user. This is the 'desk setup' — it describes the desk, not the person sitting at it. Every field in runtime config is a field that cannot travel with you. Thinner = more portable. Preferences (what you want) live in Your Memory, not here. Source: configuration-spec.md (D144).

memory_root.description: Absolute path to where Your Memory lives on this system. Your Memory is the platform — the defining property of this architecture. This tells the system where to find it on this particular deployment.

provider_adapter.description: Which adapter connects the Agent Loop to AI models. Points to an adapter config file that lists the provider profiles this adapter reaches (base URL and API key reference for each). Switching between listed profiles is an owner preference and does not touch this value (D193). Only a provider in a new format means changing this value and providing a new adapter config file. Nothing else in the system changes.

auth_mode.description: How authentication works in this deployment. Architecture default is 'local' (auth on hardware the owner controls). Implementations may define additional modes. Auth is cross-cutting (D60) — independent of the Gateway and Agent Loop.

tool_sources.description: Filesystem paths where the system finds installed tool-source descriptors. The Agent Loop scans these paths at startup, reads manifests and built-in definitions, and asks reachable configured services what tools they offer. An unavailable remote source does not block local startup and can be queried later. Tools self-describe (D146, D196); config says where to find them, not what they are. Separate services do not register through the Gateway API.
